question: Should Gateway support scheme-level browser-origin wildcards such as `chrome-extension://*`, and should that syntax live in `allowedOrigins` or a constrained pattern field?
rationale: The source failure is clear, but the requested behavior widens a browser-origin authorization boundary and related PRs do not settle the permanent wildcard grammar or audit posture.

options.title: Define constrained pattern contract
options.body: Add a reviewed pattern grammar with negative security tests, docs, and audit behavior before implementing wildcard origin matching.

options.title: Keep exact origins only
options.body: Continue with exact opaque-origin fixes and close the changing-extension-ID wildcard request as outside the current Gateway origin policy.

options.title: Allow only `chrome-extension://*`
options.body: Accept the user-facing syntax narrowly for Chrome extension origins with scheme-specific matching and regression coverage.

recommendation.title: Define constrained pattern contract
recommendation.body: Add a reviewed pattern grammar with negative security tests, docs, and audit behavior before implementing wildcard origin matching.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history on the Gateway origin hardening path and existing wildcard policy.
